mappings: Ink already proposes source-bound small-helper unfolding with static carrier width, ownership and call-frequency ranking. These are ordering heuristics only; exact equality and source application replay remain required.

Existing module composes helper unfolding with new physical/scoped capabilities derived from the CHECKED rewritten core. This matches the LLVM lesson that prior lexical/analysis summaries must invalidate after rewriting.

Applications are capped to one per caller and 32 total; helper bodies are bounded to 64 nodes and proposals to 8 by default. These local bounds do not alone establish a cumulative module code-growth guarantee across planner states.

Direct recursion is excluded. General mutually recursive summary/family budgets and argument-signature specialization are separate future work; this module is unfolding, not a complete interprocedural constant-propagation engine.

The real test checks nested binders, affine carriers, source proof rejection after rehashing a false body, composed plan replay and stale capability rejection. It does not benchmark generated execution or establish whole-backend correctness.
next: Reuse the existing proof-bound unfolding/composition machinery when designing general specialization and family cost models; do not create a backend name-pattern shortcut.
